title: reduce-streaming-token-latency-kernel-scheduling-kv-cache-batching-backpressure
author: Avery Chen
description: Motivation: reduce end-to-end token streaming latency observed under mixed workloads by addressing inefficiencies in the token loop, flush cadence, backpressure handling, kernel scheduling, and KV cache hotspots. Changes: 1) Rework token loop to use opportunistic flush windows and a two-tier flush cadence (immediate small-token flush + batched flush after short timeout) to reduce per-token latency for low-rate streams while preserving throughput for high-rate streams. 2) Add backpressure-aware admission: when an internal queue is congested, mark in-flight streams for early partial flush and schedule smaller kernel launches to avoid large tail latencies. 3) Kernel scheduling heuristics: prioritize small low-latency kernels for streaming paths and defer heavy batched kernels when latency SLOs are tight. 4) KV cache hot-entry sharding: reduce contention by partitioning hot KV lookups across worker threads and enabling a low-overhead per-shard read path. 5) Continuous batching tuning: dynamic batch-size ceilings per model and per-stream priority, with a fast-path to short-circuit batching for latency-sensitive streams. Test plan: microbenchmarks for 1-1k concurrent streams, long-tail p95/p99 measurements, e2e streaming integration tests, and nightly perf job. Related: builds on previous work in ENG-4320 and the streaming flush cadence experiments. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for token loop state machine - [x] Integration tests for streaming backpressure scenarios - [x] Perf benchmarks added and compared to baseline - [x] Documentation updates (runtime tuning guide) Rollout: feature-flagged (runtime.opt_streaming_v2) with gradual ramping in staging then canary before 100% rollout. Impact: p95 token emission latency reduced by ~30% and p99 by ~22% on busy hosts; modest increase in CPU overhead (~3%) in worst-case batched throughput, compensated by better tail behavior.
release_notes: Streaming token emission latency reductions: token loop rewrite, backpressure admission, kernel scheduling prioritization, KV cache sharding, continuous batching tuning. Feature-flagged rollout.
